card.name: Subject word after a fraction or odds phrase
card.fires_on: The noun or verb right after a phrase giving a fraction, odds or half-of-a-group figure, such as "Only one in five" or "half of experimental animals". It also fires on "of" after "a 50% chance".

modes.label: After "one in five"
modes.description: The word "patients" right after a one-in-N proportion in NSAID warning text.
modes.example: Only one in five<< patients>> who develop a serious upper GI adverse event

modes.label: Half of animals
modes.description: The verb after a phrase about half of a group of test animals.
modes.example: The oral dosage at which half of experimental animals<< are>> estimated to die is 31 times

modes.label: Chance of
modes.description: The word "of" after a percent chance.
modes.example: women aged 19–26 have about a 50% chance<< of>> becoming pregnant during a given menstrual cycle,

card.writes: The promoted tokens all mean random or randomly, so the pole suppresses a sense of chance or probability in the next word.
card.plain: It marks the word that follows a statement of odds or a share of a group, like "one in five patients" or "a 50% chance of".
